subject: Re: POC scope re-baseline for AcmeCorp
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Gomez <alyssa.gomez@acme.com>, Ben Cho <ben.cho@acme.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC follow-up & success criteria (next steps)

Hi Alyssa / Ben —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned on scope and what success looks like for the 6-week POC: 

1) Primary use case (V1):
- In-product summarization + call-summary generation for customer support (avg. 2–6k tokens per request).
- Success criteria: 85% extractive accuracy on our eval prompt set, end-to-end latency < 600ms p50, and cost < $0.003 per 1k tokens (target).

2) Secondary use case (V2):
- Private embeddings index for knowledge retrieval (10k docs, expect 200 queries/hour).
- Success criteria: mean reciprocal rank (MRR) > 0.45 on sample queries.

3) Evaluation plan & timeline: 
- Week 0 (this week): confirm POC contacts, dataset export, and infra choices.
- Week 1–2: infra & model onboarding (small test runs).
- Week 3–4: run eval prompts + integration smoke tests.
- Week 5: iterate on prompt/quantization and run final evals.
- Week 6: handoff + brief exec review.

4) Owners:
- Acme product: Alyssa (POC sponsor)
- Acme eng: Ben (technical owner)
- Redwood: Marissa (sales lead), Camila (CS/enablement), Dev (solution engineer)

5) Immediate asks: 
- Alyssa/Ben: confirm the two success criteria above or propose changes by EOD Thu.
- Ben: share a sanitized sample support transcript (5–10 examples) and an export of the KB you want embedded.
- Procurement: expected timeline for simple SOW/PO (if needed).

I’ve attached the proposed POC roadmap (Acme_POC_Roadmap_v2.pdf) and a short checklist. If we get confirmation on the criteria and dataset this week, we’ll aim to start infra onboarding Monday.

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0102
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Acme_POC_Roadmap_v2.pdf
From: Alyssa Gomez <alyssa.gomez@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Cho <ben.cho@acme.com>, Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC follow-up & success criteria (next steps)

Thanks Marissa — this looks good and appreciated the clear timeline. A couple of quick items: 

- We can confirm the primary summarization criteria (accuracy + latency). For cost, Ben and I want to keep an eye on the delta vs our current vendor — can you include expected cost ranges for a few batching/quantization configs?
- Important: we want to add one more evaluation axis mid-POC — redaction/compliance detection on transcripts (PII redaction accuracy). This is critical for our regulated vertical. Can we add that as a scoped V1.5 and track it alongside the summarization tests?

Ben will upload the sample transcripts by EOD today. Procurement: we should be able to circulate a simple SOW by next week — I’ll ping once I have dates.

—Alyssa
Alyssa Gomez | Head of Product, AcmeCorp
alyssa.gomez@acme.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Gomez <alyssa.gomez@acme.com>
Cc: Ben Cho <ben.cho@acme.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Jun 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC follow-up & success criteria (next steps)

Alyssa — great catch on the redaction requirement. Proposed re-baseline below (I’m calling it a V1.5 addition so we’re explicit about impact):

What’s changing: add redaction/compliance detector for transcripts as a parallel eval. Test surface: 500 labeled spans across 50 transcripts we’ll use for PII redaction recall/precision.

Impact to timeline: +1 week to the POC schedule (move final exec review to end of Week 7) if we run redaction labeling and iterations during Weeks 3–4. If Acme can provide pre-labeled samples, we can keep the original 6-week end date.

Impact to success criteria: add metric — PII redaction recall >= 90% and precision >= 88% (target).

Next steps I propose:
- Ben to share transcripts (raw) by EOD Thu (thanks).
- Camila to scope labeling support and estimate time/cost if Acme needs help.
- Dev to validate that model variant and K/V caching will not break redaction pipeline and to propose batching knobs.
- Marissa to update the POC roadmap and send revised SOW language noting the V1.5 addition.

If everyone is OK with V1.5, I’ll send an updated roadmap + a short change note for procurement (SOW addendum) by Friday.

Thanks —
Marissa

Attachment: (will send updated roadmap after confirmation)
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Alyssa Gomez <alyssa.gomez@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 10:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC follow-up & success criteria (next steps)

Quick technical note on the redaction evaluation:

- We can run redaction detection as a lightweight classification head on top of the same encoder used for summarization to avoid separate inference passes. That keeps cost down but will require a small labeled set for fine-tuning (~500 examples).
- If Acme cannot provide labeled data, Redwood can spin labeling support (Camila — estimate pending) and run an initial zero-shot pass to set expectations.
- Performance consideration: enabling the classifier will add ~40–70ms p50 per request if run inline; we can measure that on small runs and report back.

Action: I’ll run a quick bench on our dedicated dev pool and share a short table of latency/cost for three configs (no classifier / inline classifier / batched classifier) by Thursday.

—Dev
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
